title: Secondary Survey & Handover (SAMPLE, MIST)
summary: Once life threats are dealt with: check the casualty head to toe, take a SAMPLE history, record observations and times, and hand over clearly.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if anything found is serious
when: Any life-threatening problem found – go back to the primary survey
Changes in breathing, response or skin colour

steps.title: Primary survey first
steps.text: Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation must be sorted first.

steps.title: Head-to-toe check
steps.text: With consent and gloves, look and feel gently from head to toe for bleeding, swelling, deformity, wounds and pain. Tell them what you are doing.

steps.title: SAMPLE history
points: E – Events leading up to the incident

steps.title: Record observations
steps.text: Note level of response (AVPU), breathing rate, skin colour/temperature and pulse if trained, with the time. Repeat regularly.

steps.title: Hand over (MIST)
steps.text: When help arrives, give a short, structured handover:
points: M – Mechanism of injury / what happened
I – Injuries found or illness suspected
S – Signs: observations and how they have changed
T – Treatment given and times (tourniquet time, naloxone, aspirin)

doNot: Do not move a casualty unnecessarily to examine them
Do not forget to record times
Do not delay calling for help to complete a full survey

sources.title: American Red Cross First Aid/CPR/AED Participant's Manual
sources.section: Checking an injured or ill person

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
